examples.ko: 뇌세포는 한번 죽으면 다시 살아나기 어렵대요.
examples.en: They say brain cells are hard to bring back once they die.
We looked at a picture of brain cells in science class.
Brain cells were damaged in the accident.

examples.ko: 새로운 걸 배우면 뇌세포가 자극을 받아요.
examples.en: Learning something new stimulates your brain cells.
Each brain cell sends and receives signals from the others.

examples.ko: 머리를 너무 썼더니 뇌세포가 다 죽은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I used my head so much that it feels like all my brain cells died.

explain: 과학 이야기에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 우스갯소리로 '뇌세포가 죽다'라고 많이 말해요. 어이없는 일이나 너무 힘든 공부를 했을 때 쓰는 농담이에요. 비슷한 말로 '신경세포'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 어려운 시험을 봤더니 뇌세포가 죽는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: After taking a hard exam, it feels like my brain cells are dying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 힘든 공부를 했을 때 쓰는 우스갯소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking phrase for when studying or thinking was very hard.

phrases.en: Nerve cells carry signals in the brain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뇌와 몸의 신경을 이루는 세포로, 과학 설명에서 주로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cells that make up the brain and nerves; mostly used in scientific explanations.

phrases.nuance_ko: 머리를 쓰게 하는 활동을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe activities that make you think.

explain_en: It is used in science, but in daily life people joke '뇌세포가 죽다' (my brain cells died) after something absurd or exhausting studying. A related term is '신경세포' (nerve cell).

examples.ko: 어린이는 보호자를 동반해야 입장할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Children can enter only when accompanied by a guardian.
They came to the event with their parents.

examples.ko: 이 병은 열을 동반하는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: This illness often comes with a fever.
Typhoons bring heavy rain along with them.
I went on a business trip with my family.
I asked whether I could bring a friend.

explain: 사람과 같이 가는 것뿐 아니라 '비를 동반한 바람', '열을 동반한 기침'처럼 어떤 일과 함께 나타난다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요. 친구와 같이 갈 때 일상 대화에서는 '같이 가다', '데리고 가다'가 자연스러워요. 동반하다는 안내문, 뉴스, 설명문에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This illness comes with severe pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일과 함께 나타나는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that appears together with another thing.

phrases.en: You may bring your family to the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 데리고 간다는 뜻으로 안내문에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to bring someone along, often seen in notices.

phrases.en: It's more fun when you go together with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 동반하다 대신 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This sounds more natural than 동반하다 in daily conversation.

explain_en: Besides going along with a person, it is often used for something that appears together with something else, as in '비를 동반한 바람' (wind with rain) or '열을 동반한 기침' (a cough with fever). In daily talk, 같이 가다 or 데리고 가다 sounds more natural for going with a friend. 동반하다 shows up in notices, news, and explanations.

examples.en: That child has distinct facial features.

examples.ko: 이목구비가 뚜렷한 얼굴이라 사진이 잘 나와요.
examples.en: With such defined features, she looks good in photos.
My younger sister's features look a lot like our mother's.
The model has bold, open features.

examples.ko: 이 인형은 이목구비를 아주 섬세하게 표현했어요.
examples.en: This doll has very delicately drawn facial features.
The painter carefully drew the person's features.

explain: 귀·눈·입·코, 곧 얼굴 생김새를 통틀어 '이목구비'라고 해요. 보통 '이목구비가 뚜렷하다'처럼 또렷하고 시원하게 생겼다고 말할 때 써요. 얼굴 전체의 모양은 '얼굴형', 눈의 모양은 '눈매'라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.example: 언니는 이목구비가 뚜렷해서 화장이 잘 받아요.
phrases.en: My older sister has clear features, so makeup looks good on her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴 생김새가 또렷하고 시원할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for features that look clear and well defined.

phrases.en: That actor has neat, well-shaped features.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈, 코, 입이 단정하고 바르게 생겼다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to praise eyes, nose and mouth as neat and well proportioned.

phrases.en: I drew the eyes, nose and mouth on the doll's face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 인형에 눈, 코, 입을 그려 넣을 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use this when drawing eyes, nose and mouth on a picture or doll.

explain_en: 이목구비 covers the ears, eyes, mouth and nose together, in other words the features of a face. It is most often used in 이목구비가 뚜렷하다, meaning clear and well-defined features. The overall shape of the face is 얼굴형, and the shape of the eyes is 눈매.

en: to be dim; to be poorly lit

examples.ko: 눈이 침침해서 작은 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My eyes are blurry, so I can't see small print well.
The room is dim, so I'll turn on the light.
Lately my eyes keep getting blurry.
A dim alley is scary to walk through at night.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어서 눈이 침침하다고 할머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said her eyes have gotten blurry with age.

examples.ko: 침침할 때는 눈을 잠깐 쉬게 해 주세요.
examples.en: When your eyes feel blurry, let them rest for a moment.

explain: '눈이 침침하다'는 시력이 흐릿하고 답답할 때 자주 쓰고, 어두침침한 장소에도 써요. 그냥 '어둡다'보다 흐릿하고 답답한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: My eyes are blurry because I read until late at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시력이 흐릿하고 답답할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, for blurry and heavy-feeling eyesight.

phrases.example: 침침한 방에서 책을 읽으면 눈에 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: Reading in a dim room is bad for your eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이에요. 불빛이 약하고 흐린 곳에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form for a place with weak, murky light.

phrases.en: The hallway is gloomy and dim, so it's a little scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어둡다'와 합쳐서 어둡고 흐린 장소를 더 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '어둡다' to stress a dark and murky place.

explain_en: '눈이 침침하다' is often used when your eyesight feels hazy and heavy, and it can also describe a gloomy place. It has a hazier, stuffier feel than simply '어둡다' (dark).
